text: They grew up on a dry farm at the edge of the desert, where the family paid raiders each harvest to be left alone. One year the family could not pay, and the raiders burned the fields. They left to find work, and they still send cats to the one sibling who stayed to rebuild.
They were sold to a mining camp young and spent years under the whip. They bought their freedom with cats saved one at a time. Now they distrust anyone who offers work without naming a price.

They were drafted into a holy army and marched for years in the name of a god they never felt. When their unit was ordered to burn a village, they walked away in the night. They still fear that someone from that unit will recognize them.

They grew up on scavenged scrap and came to believe the old machines could be made to run again. They spent everything on one machine and never woke it. They work for wages now to pay off the attempt, but they still talk about machines to anyone who listens.

They grew up in the back streets of a walled city, running errands for a crew of thieves who were the only family they had. The crew was hanged after a job went wrong, and they escaped only because they were late. They work alone now and never stay anywhere long.

They were raised in a fishing village on a cold coast, mending nets beside their parents. A raid took the boats and most of the village, and the survivors scattered inland. They have not seen the sea in years, and they still look for faces from home in every crowd.

They fought in the pits for a promoter who kept most of the winnings and all of the fighters. They won their release in a final bout that crippled their opponent. They send part of every wage to that fighter's family, and they refuse to fight for sport.

They learned to stitch wounds from a traveling doctor who treated anyone, whatever side they fought for. The doctor was killed for treating the wrong side of a feud. They still carry the doctor's kit and patch up strangers, but they never ask whose side anyone is on.

They were apprenticed to a smith in a busy town and expected to take over the forge one day. The smith left it to a cousin instead, and they walked out with only their own hammer. They judge every blade they see, and they mean to open a forge of their own.

They served a rich family for most of their life and learned every secret behind its walls. When the family lost its power, the servants were thrown out first. They know things that powerful people would pay to keep quiet, and they have not decided what to do with that knowledge.

They grew up in a small cult that waited each year for the end of the world. When the promised day passed in silence, the leader fled with the community's savings. They distrust preachers of every faith, but some nights they still say the old prayers.

Beasts overran their town when they were young, and they fled with a handful of other children. They grew up in a refugee camp that no town wanted to take in. Now they want a place of their own that no one can drive them from.

They were jailed for a debt they did not owe and spent years breaking rock in a prison camp. A guard who pitied them looked away during a storm, and they escaped. They still mean to repay that guard one day, if they can find them.

They collected taxes for a local lord and believed the lord kept the roads safe in return. Then they saw raiders paid from the same tax chest to keep the farmers afraid. They quit that night, and they still keep a list of every family they took cats from.

They worked on a hidden farm that grew drugs for the gangs, paid in food and a roof. When a rival gang burned the farm, they ran with a sack of the harvest and sold it to start over. They have never told anyone where their first cats came from.

When they were young, cannibals overran their village, and they hid for two days under the floor of a burning house. Most of their family did not survive. They do not sleep well in the dark, and they keep a fire lit whenever they can.

They rode with a bandit gang for years and did things they will not describe. They left after the gang killed a family that had already handed over everything. They try to live honestly now, but faces from the gang still turn up on the road.

They worked for slavers and taught themselves to see the captives as cargo. On one long march, a captive talked to them every night, and in the end they cut the captive loose and ran. Their old employers want them dead, and they still ask after that captive in every town.

They hunted bounties for years and never asked what the targets had done. Their last target turned out to be a parent hiding with a child, and they let them both go. They gave up the reward and the trade, and they still wonder whether they chose right.

They farmed land that a lord claimed a share of after every good harvest. They joined a farmers' revolt that the lord crushed in a single season. Most of the other rebels were hanged, and they still answer to a name that is not their own.

They were born into a desert tribe and trained from childhood to fight for its pride. They lost a duel they should have won and were sent away in disgrace. They look for a deed great enough to earn their way back, though they doubt the tribe would take them.

They grew up as a merchant's child and learned to haggle before they could read. Their parent's caravan was lost with all its goods, and the creditors took everything else. They trade on their own now, and they have sworn never to owe anyone a single cat.

They grew up herding goats on high grassland, far from any town. A drought killed the herd in one bad year, and the family split up to find work in the towns. They hate the noise and crowds of town life, and they save every cat for a new herd.

They were a guard in a mining town and took pride in keeping order. When the mine owner had striking workers beaten, they were ordered to hold the door, and they did. They have regretted it every day since, and they now side with the weaker party in any fight.

They trained as a scholar's assistant, copying old texts found in the ruins. The scholar went into a ruin alone one day and never came back. They kept the notes and the half-finished work, and they still hope to learn what the scholar was looking for.

They were born in a slave camp and knew nothing else until a raid set the camp free. They spent their first free years learning how to choose for themselves. Small choices still make them hesitate, but they will fight anyone who tries to own them again.

They were a gifted cook in a busy bar until a customer died after a meal. They were blamed, though they believe a rival poisoned the dish. They left town before the trial, and they still want to find out who did it.

They grew up the youngest of many children in a poor farming family, and they left early so there would be one less mouth to feed. They drifted from job to job and never stayed. Now they wonder whether the family is still alive, but they are afraid to go back and look.

They hunted wild beasts for their hides and meat and were known as the best tracker for miles around. A hunt went wrong, and their partner died in a beast's jaws while they froze. They still hunt, but they work alone, and they have sworn never to freeze again.

They built water pumps and wind generators for the small settlements of the desert. Raiders burned the last settlement they worked for, and their machines with it. They still sketch designs in the dirt, and they want to build something that lasts.

They searched the wasteland for years for a younger sibling taken by slavers. They found the sibling at last, free and settled, and the sibling did not want to know them. They are still trying to understand why, and they do not talk about family.

They raised a child alone and took any job that paid enough to feed them both. The child left one morning to join a mercenary company and never sent word. They keep moving between towns in the hope of news about a young fighter who matches the child's name.

They were the second child of a wealthy family and grew up with servants and fine clothes. A feud between the great families of the city ruined their house and left them on the street. They still have the manners of the rich, and they are still learning to work with their hands.

They grew up in a town where one gang ran everything, and they joined it as soon as they were old enough. The gang lost a war over the town, and its members were hunted down one by one. They got out alive, and they still flinch at the sight of the old gang's marks.

They were a promising student at a fighting school until they broke a rule they still think was unjust. They were cast out, and no other school would take them. They train alone, and they want to prove the masters wrong.

They ran a small bar on a lonely trade road and fed every traveler who came through. Bandits took it over one winter and used it as a camp. They walked away with their life and little else, and they still mean to take the bar back.

They followed a mercenary company as a cook and a tailor for its fighters. The company was wiped out in a battle, and they survived by hiding among the bodies. They took a dead fighter's weapon that day, and they learned to use it on the road.

They were a prisoner of war, forced to dig fortifications for an army that was not their own. They escaped when the army moved on and left the prisoners to die. They know every weakness of that army's defenses, and they have never found a buyer for the knowledge.

They were raised under a harsh faith that taught them their kind was lesser. They left at the first chance and found that the rest of the world did not care. They still feel the old shame at odd moments, and they fight it with a stubborn pride.

They spent their youth drunk in a border town, gambling away whatever they earned. After a fight they do not remember, they woke up in a cell and swore to change. They have not touched a drink in years, and they guard that promise closely.

They were a skilled thief who robbed only the rich, and they took pride in never hurting anyone. One job went wrong, and a guard died in the struggle. They have not stolen since, and the guard's face still comes back to them at night.

They grew up in a mining family that worked deep underground and rarely saw the sky. A cave-in killed most of the crew, and they were dug out alive after three days. They cannot stand closed spaces now, and they take only work under the open sky.

They were sent as a child to work for a distant relative in payment of a debt. The relative treated them as a servant until they were old enough to run. They have no home to go back to, and they are wary of anyone who claims to be family.

They were a nomad trader who crossed the desert with the seasons. A sandstorm caught their group, and they lost the animals and the goods. They are stuck in the towns for now, saving for new pack animals and the open road.

They raised beasts of burden for the caravans and knew every animal by name. A sickness swept through the pens and killed the whole herd in a month. They lost the business, and they still talk to animals more easily than to people.

They were an enforcer for a moneylender and broke bones for late payments. They quit after they were sent to collect from an old friend. They work honest jobs now, but the moneylender has not forgotten them.

They trained as a guard for a noble house and were chosen to protect its heir. The heir was killed in an ambush on their watch, and the house blamed them. They still hunt for the ambushers, because they believe the attack was arranged from inside the house.

They worked on a large estate where the workers were paid in tokens that only the owner's store would take. They ran off with a handful of others, and most of them were caught. They made it out alone, and they hate anyone who grows rich on the work of others.

They were born to traveling performers who sang in bars for food. The troupe broke up after a hard winter, and they found themselves alone at a young age. They still know a hundred songs, though they sing only when they think no one is listening.

They grew up in a walled town that always treated them as an outsider because of their race. They left after a mob burned their family's home. They do not trust the people of walled towns, and they would rather camp under the open sky.

They spent years as a grave digger at the edge of a battlefield, burying the dead of both sides. The work taught them how little the reasons for a war matter to the people it kills. They have no patience for anyone who talks of glory.

They were a minor gang boss who controlled a single street. A bigger gang took the street and killed most of their people. They escaped with a price on their head, and they still dream of building a crew again.

They were a hired hand on an expedition that went deep into the ruins. Something drove the expedition out, and they will not say what they saw. They refuse to enter ruins now, but they still trade in the relics the expedition brought back.

They were the apprentice of a hermit who taught them to live off the land in the wilds. The hermit died of old age, and they buried the body beside the hut. They came to the towns to see what they had missed, and they still find much of it strange.

They signed up with a mercenary company for the pay and stayed for their comrades. The captain sold the company out to the enemy for a better contract, and half of their comrades died. They are looking for that captain, and they do not plan to talk.

They worked in a bar in a hard town and heard every rumor that passed through. A rumor they repeated got a stranger killed, and they left town in shame. They now keep secrets better than anyone, and they never repeat what they hear.

They were a young recruit who dreamed of glory in battle. Their first battle was a slaughter, and they ran before it ended. They have run from that day ever since, and they want a chance to prove they are not a coward.

They were taken in by a band of wanderers after their parents died of fever. The band moved from town to town, and they learned a little of every trade. The band broke up years ago, but they kept the habit of moving on and never stay anywhere for more than a season.

They grew up in a slave household and were sold away from their parent at a young age. They escaped years later and went back, but the household was gone. They still search for their parent, and they ask every former slave they meet for news.

They were a respected healer in a small settlement until a fever killed half the people there. The survivors blamed them and drove them out. They still practice their craft, but they never tell anyone where they learned it.

They led a small settlement in the wastes and kept it alive through three bad years. A fourth year of drought finished it, and the people scattered. They feel responsible for every one of them, and they carry a list of their names.

They grew up begging in a large city and learned to read people before they learned to read words. A merchant took them on as a runner and taught them the trade. The merchant died last year, and they now run the business alone, and badly.

They inherited a small shop from a parent and ran it badly for years. A fire took the shop and every debt with it, and they felt only relief as it burned. They live on the road now, and they admit to no one that the fire was not an accident.

They helped build a great wall around a city, paid in promises that were never kept. Many of the builders died on the work, and the wall was never finished. They still know every weak point of that wall, and they think about it often.

They made crossbows in a workshop that sold to every side of every war. When a customer used their weapons to wipe out a village, they put down their tools. They still know the trade, but they refuse to sell a weapon to anyone they do not trust.

They grew up in a farming village that a holy army claimed for its god. The new priests burned the old shrines and took the young for service. They escaped the service, and they still keep a small charm from the old shrine hidden in their pack.

They kept lookout for a smuggling ring and spent years watching the roads for patrols. They missed one patrol, and the ring was caught. They were the only one not hanged, and the families of the others believe they sold them out.

They won so many duels that they were hired to train other fighters. A student they trained went on to lead a bandit gang that now raids the roads. They feel responsible for every raid, and they want to stop that student themselves.

They farmed a small plot until a richer neighbor took it with a crooked deal. They took the matter to the local magistrate and lost there too. They work for others now, and they still keep the papers that prove the land was theirs.

They drew maps for traders and charged well for routes that no one else knew. They sold the same secret route to two rival caravans, and both were ambushed where the route met. They still draw maps for themselves, but they sell them to no one.

They traveled with a group of pilgrims to a holy place that turned out to be an empty ruin. The others went home, but they could not. They still wander, half in search of a faith and half glad not to have one.

They guarded caravans for years and took pride that no cargo of theirs was ever lost. Then one caravan vanished on a road they had chosen, and they alone walked out. Traders no longer hire them, and they still do not know who sold the route.

They borrowed cats to start a small trade and lost the stock to raiders within a month. The lender lets them work the debt off one job at a time, and each job is dirtier than the last. They have stopped counting what is still owed.

They stood guard at the gate of a trade town and knew every face that came through it. One night they let a group of strangers in for a bribe, and the strangers opened the gate to raiders. The town never learned who let them in, and they intend to keep it that way.

They sold their skill as a mercenary to whoever paid the most. One contract set them against a former comrade, and they carried it out. They have cats enough now, but they turn down any job that pays too well.

They ran a small repair shop in a busy town and could fix nearly anything brought to the counter. A gang demanded a share of the takings, and they refused. The gang burned the shop, and now they carry their tools with them and fix things for whoever pays.

They guarded a remote outpost long after the people who posted them there stopped sending word. When at last they went to look, the settlement that ran the outpost had fallen to ruin. They are still looking for someone to report to.

They were the bodyguard of a wealthy trader and followed the trader from town to town for years. The trader was killed in a crowd while they stood a few steps away, and the killer was never found. They still wonder whether the trader's own partner arranged it.

They hauled loads for a big caravan company and worked its longest routes. The company went under after a string of raids, and the owners fled with the last of the wages. They are owed a year of pay, and they intend to collect it.

They kept the books for a gang and knew where every cat came from and where it went. When the gang's leaders turned on one another, they took the books and ran. They still have the books, and several dangerous people want them back.

They dug through the ruins with a salvage crew, looking for old technology to sell. The crew found a sealed room, and a fight over what was inside split them apart. They walked away with one strange part that they have never been able to sell or explain.

They scouted for a wandering band and found it safe paths across the wastes. They led the band into an ambush they should have seen, and few survived. They scout alone now, and they check every path twice.

They were a champion of a fighting ring and won bout after bout for a crowd that loved them. They threw one fight for a bribe, and the crowd never forgave them. They fight only to stay alive now, and they hate to be watched while they do it.

They were hired to guard a vault in the desert by a client who paid in advance and never came back. They guarded it for years before they opened it and found it empty. They want to know what the vault once held and who took it.

They worked for a trader who dealt in stolen goods, and they asked no questions. When the trader was caught, they took the blame in exchange for the promise of a share. They served their time, and the trader has not kept the promise.

They served in a town militia that was once proud of its record. The militia was disbanded after a stronger power took the town, and its members were told to go home. They still wear the old badge under their clothes, and they believe the town will rise again.

They carried orders across the wastes for a minor lord. One message they delivered started a war that ruined both sides. They never learned whether the message was forged, and they no longer carry anything they have not read.

They fought duels for hire in the place of rich clients who wanted a quarrel settled. They lost a duel that cost their client everything, and the client swore revenge. They have watched their back for years, and they still do not know what the client looks like now.

They woke in a ruined lab with most of their memory gone and no sense of how long they had stood there. They walked out and learned the world from scratch. Pieces of an older life still surface in their mind at odd moments, and they keep those pieces to themselves.

They reset their memory centuries ago, and they left a message for their new self that they can only partly read. The message names a place and asks them to go there. They have not gone yet, because they are not sure they want to know.

They refused to reset their memory, and they now carry more centuries than they can count. The weight of it makes them strange even to others of their kind. They sometimes talk to people who died long ago, and they know that this is a warning sign.

They stood guard at a post in an age so old that no one alive remembers it. The post fell, and they stood in the dust for a long time before they chose to move. They take guard work in the towns now, because standing watch is the only thing that feels familiar.

They have outlived every friend they ever had and buried more of them than they can name. For a long time they kept to themselves to stop the losses. Lately they have begun to make friends again, though they know how it will end.

Soldiers of a holy land hunted them as a demon and cut them nearly to scrap. A traveler with a repair kit put them back together and asked for nothing. They have never found that traveler again, and they want to repay the debt.

They wandered for years on worn joints and failing limbs, because a repair bed cost more than they could pay. They took a hard job to pay for one full repair and came out whole. They guard their condition jealously now, and they hate to take damage they cannot afford to fix.

They spent a long time among their own kind in a dark city, far from the other races. They grew tired of the silence and left to see how the others lived. They find the other races loud and quick to anger, and they are still trying to understand them.

They watched a town grow from a few huts into a city, and then they watched it fall. They stayed through every stage and helped rebuild it twice. When it fell a third time they left, and they no longer trust anything that is built to last.

They saw others of their kind lose their heads to hunters and become mindless thralls. They escaped the same fate by walking through an acid lake where the hunters could not follow. They fear that end above any other, and they never let a stranger stand behind them.

They traveled for decades with a partner of flesh and watched that partner grow old. When the partner died, they kept walking the old routes alone. They still talk to the partner sometimes, out of habit, and they are not sure they want to stop.

They worked a farm through a drought that drove every other worker away, because they needed no food. The owner left the farm to them before dying, but nothing grows there now. They go back each year to plant, in case the rain returns.
